topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment options
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Marcus Reed (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Head of Security, Citrine), Maya Ortiz (Director of Platform), Liam Park (DevOps)

[00:00] Marcus: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Marcus Reed from Redwood here, with Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Jordan: Good, thanks. Quick note, I'm in EST, so it's 11 for me. We have about 45 minutes, hope that's cool.
[00:12] Marcus: Perfect. Agenda for today — quick intro, understand your security/compliance requirements for hosted vs dedicated vs private, dig into SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS, data residency and retention, and agree next steps.
[00:22] Maya: Sounds good. Mostly here because we want to understand the tradeoffs. We're evaluating a few vendors and need to be strict around audit trails and key management.
[00:30] Priya: Great. To start, can you tell us current stack and what data flow looks like? Are you sending PHI or PII to model inference, or is it strictly insurance claims metadata?
[00:40] Liam: Mostly PII — names, partial SSNs, claim notes, some attachments. We currently pseudonymize at the application layer but regulators want stronger controls. We're testing a couple of deployment modes.
[00:52] Jordan: We're SOC 2 Type II in scope for core systems, and ISO 27001 is under discussion for later this year. For any vendor access we need audit logs, SSO with SAML, SCIM provisioning, RBAC, and encryption with our KMS.
[01:05] Priya: Understood. Redwood supports SSO via SAML and OIDC, SCIM for provisioning, and RBAC with fine-grained roles. For hosted we provide audit logs and event streams; for dedicated and private you get more control over network and key management.
[01:20] Marcus: Quick clarification — when you say KMS integration, do you require customer-managed keys (CMK) in an HSM, or will envelope keys with Redwood-managed keys suffice for the initial pilot?
[01:29] Maya: For prod we'd want CMKs in a customer HSM or cloud KMS. For pilot, envelope encryption with customer-managed keys (we control the root) might be acceptable.
[01:38] Marcus: Good, that's consistent with other customers. Our Private option supports bring-your-own-KMS and HSM integration; Dedicated can be configured with customer KMS in many cloud providers. Hosted offers KMS integration for enterprise customers via a VPC/private link and customer key options.
[01:54] Jordan: How about audit logs — retention, immutability, and access control? We need logs that map requests back to users and tokens and are retained for at least 1 year, with export to our SIEM.
[02:05] Priya: Redwood's audit logs include token-level details, model used, request/response metadata (note: we redact user content by default for hosted unless configured otherwise). Logs can stream to S3, SIEM via webhook or forwarder. Retention is configurable per account; for enterprise we have long-term retention add-ons. For immutability, we support WORM buckets and signed logs.
[02:23] Liam: A couple of notes — we need low latency. Our main product calls the model for real-time chat. Latency vs cost tradeoffs are a concern.
[02:31] Marcus: Yep that's the typical tradeoff. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latency for steady workloads; hosted is easiest but can have more variability. Private on-prem gives max control at higher ops cost.
[02:44] Jordan: Any certifications you can share? SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 cert? Also penetration test results or pen test summary?
[02:52] Priya: We can share our SOC 2 Type II report and ISO scope summary. Pen test summaries are available under an NDA; we also provide our bug-bounty program metrics. We'll attach those to the follow-up.
[03:03] Marcus: We'll put those in the doc pack — SOC2, ISO scope, pen test summary, compliance whitepaper.
[03:09] Jordan: On SSO — SAML 2.0 is a must. We also want SCIM provisioning for accounts and groups, and roles mapped to our groups.
[03:17] Priya: We support SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM 2.0. You can map SAML attributes to RBAC roles; we also support just-in-time provisioning or SCIM syncing. For Dedicated and Private you can lock down to an IP range and require mTLS for admin APIs.
[03:31] Maya: Good. How do you handle RBAC granularity? We want separate roles for developer, ops, security, with different permissions around data export and key management.
[03:40] Priya: RBAC is role-and-permission based: you can define custom roles, limit model deployment permissions, and restrict data export or download. Audit events capture role-assigned actions. There's a UI plus API for role management.
[03:51] Liam: About data residency — some claims data needs to stay in us-east-1 or on-prem. Does Redwood offer region locking?
[03:57] Marcus: Yes, region pinning is supported for redwood-hosted and dedicated; Private obviously keeps data where you install. For hosted we can pin customer's workspace to a region and ensure logs and storage stay there.
[04:10] Jordan: Encryption in transit and at rest? Are keys rotated automatically?
[04:14] Priya: TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit; at rest we encrypt using AES-256. Key rotation is supported via KMS policies; if you bring your own keys, rotation is under your KMS policy. Redwood supports envelope encryption and customer-provided root keys.
[04:29] Jordan: Any demo of the audit UI?
[04:32] Priya: We can do a UI demo in the technical deep dive. Today I can describe the events: user sign-in, token use, API call with model ID, request hash, response size — all have timestamps and request IDs.
[04:45] Maya: One concern — if we're using hosted, how much of PII leaves our VPC? We prefer not to send raw attachments out without additional redaction.
[04:53] Marcus: For hosted we have three data flow options: 1) redact and pseudonymize at app layer then send, 2) use a private link/VPC peering and customer-managed encryption keys so data is segregated, 3) dedicated/private where data never traverses public internet. We can support additional preprocessing to strip attachments or send only embeddings.
[05:15] Jordan: Regarding logs mapping back to users — we need to show audit trails for compliance audits. Will Redwood produce tamper-evident logs?
[05:22] Priya: We support log signing (HMAC) and export to WORM S3 for tamper resistance; Hash chains for log files are possible if you want immutable audit trails.
[05:32] Liam: For pilot, we want to run a 2-week bench on dedicated with a 100 TPS spike to see KV cache behavior and latencies. Can Redwood run that?
[05:42] Marcus: Absolutely. For POC workloads we can spin up a small dedicated pool, run a benchmark harness — Priya will lead on the checklist. We'll need sample payloads and expected SLAs.
[05:52] Maya: Ok, timeline — compliance signoff needs to happen in 6 weeks. If we can get SOC2 docs and a benchmark by next week, procurement can start.
[06:02] Marcus: Sounds feasible. We'll aim to get docs by tomorrow and schedule the deep dive next week.
[06:08] Jordan: A couple of specific questions: 1) Does Redwood store raw prompt/response data by default? 2) Can we opt out of storage or have automatic deletion policies?
[06:16] Priya: By default hosted keeps request logs and short-term request/response data for debugging; you can opt out of content retention, enable redaction, or set automatic deletion policies. In Dedicated/Private you control retention and can disable storage entirely.
[06:28] Jordan: Great. For SOC 2 auditors, we also need attestation on third-party subprocessors and data flow diagrams.
[06:35] Marcus: We'll include a subprocessors list and a high-level data flow diagram in the pack.
[06:40] Maya: Regarding SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints — we need sample configs to show to our IdP team.
[06:46] Priya: We'll share SAML metadata, SCIM schema, and sample SAML attribute mappings.
[06:51] Marcus: Any blockers from your side for doing a dedicated POC? Cost is usually the sticking point.
[06:57] Maya: Cost and contractual terms — e.g., data processing addendum, liability limits. We'll have procurement review once security is happy.
[07:06] Jordan: Competitors — we're also looking at OpenAI + private infra, and a managed Sagemaker approach for private inference. Need to compare unit economics and security controls.
[07:15] Marcus: Understood. We'll include a TCO comparison for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with likely cost ranges.
[07:20] Liam: One last technical — how does Redwood handle model updates and versioning? We need pinned model versions for reproducible outputs during audits.
[07:28] Priya: We support model version pinning, immutable model snapshots for canary/rollouts, and a model catalog with performance profiles. You can pin production routes to a specific version and get diff reports on model outputs.
[07:40] Jordan: Good. That helps with our eval criteria.
[07:44] Marcus: Ok we're at about 40 minutes. Recap and next steps: Marcus to send SOC2/ISO docs and subprocessors list by 2026-03-19; Priya to schedule technical deep dive and bench checklist for week of 2026-03-23; Redwood to share dedicated pricing and TCO; Citrine to share data retention policy and IdP contacts.
[07:59] Maya: Yep, that matches. We'll also prepare sample payloads for the benchmark.
[08:05] Marcus: Perfect. Any final questions?
[08:08] Jordan: Nothing else, thanks.
[08:10] Marcus: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc pack and calendar invite.

Notes / occasional transcription artifacts: 'Sagemaker' sometimes heard as 'sage-maker' in audio, 'KV cache' mis-transcribed as 'K V cash' in one segment, 'SCIM' sometimes expanded to 'skim' by the auto-transcriber.

End of transcript.
